title: M7.P5: Define category validation and explicit cloud actions
body:
## Current qualification — source-overlay UI complete

Published [final evidence and handoff](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/blob/d5e2f78618624cad919afaba6784bef3f7eaf8c7/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-07-cloud-validator/ui/README.md) at distribution next `d5e2f78618624cad919afaba6784bef3f7eaf8c7`; remote readback verified. Product source remains clean and local/unintegrated: distribution `6f89bc7cecee5972909828103689e2c7c0711c30`, ES `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e`. #512 localized failure/check-busy wording, #513 small-panel help/editor fit and #514 selected-folder empty guidance are fixed and qualified in that ES source. Their inclusion is explicitly tracked here under #508; no pin or installed device changed.

The final UI index has **99 entries: 89 reviewed screenshots, nine rejected screenshots retained, and CF10 final firmware/public adoption pending**. It includes positive scan-to-supported-systems/back, empty-selected/populated-other-library refusal, all changed help variants, interrupted/failed/retried checks, selective folder creation, OAuth UI and restore-finish callbacks. Exact source/catalog identities and explicit unchanged-input reuse are retained. Root verified the full inventory before retiring the guest/compiler, independently confirmed resource absence and all worker seals, and retained 529 final sealed files. Cleanup reclaimed4.86GiB. No build, VM or audit job remains active in this lane.

Full host regression remains **1,311 top-level PASS**, zeroFAIL/SKIP; ordinary VM WebDAV/SFTP each **108 PASS**. #512 unit logic passes183cases/4752assertions; later text-only fixes have separate compile/link/syntax/catalog/vocabulary proof. Existing accepted candidate16/device firmware and the78-frame baseline remain unchanged. The required D-WORKFLOW-155/156 flow-and-reviewed-screenshot process is published in both agent entrypoints, the canonical UI rule and the evidence-index schema. A mechanical title/index check is not semantic screenshot coverage.

**Remaining order:** #510's unanswered release-scope choice for small-file repair → #508 qualified source/pin integration → #507 frozen independent post-candidate16 audit → assembled firmware/public ROCKNIX and clean-install qualification, source/licence and named physical gates. The validator direction is settled; generic save-file organization is not implemented and must not be silently claimed. No new external audit, device build or personal-cloud action has occurred.

- [x] Required flow/screenshot process is institutionalized in both agent entrypoints and the canonical UI rule; commit f6037a9133 and the published checkpoint above provide the artifact. Final cloud-flow coverage remains a separate open criterion.

## Required UI change protocol — 2026-10-08

> If we don't have it institutionalized already as a required process, we need to make sure that any time we make any change to EmulationStation or any part of our information architecture (or even screen content), we update the flow and then the accompanying screenshot for the flow. This is going to be increasingly critical as we work on automated testing.

D-WORKFLOW-156 makes this required before completion or product-pin promotion: review every ES change's affected experience; update canonical menu/IA/flow references and their reviewed happy-path/branch screenshots, including copy and script-supplied content changes. A nonvisual change names the exercised flow and proves its presentation remains unchanged. Keep a machine-readable evidence-index.json with stable flow/branch IDs, trigger/outcome, exact source/build, locale/panel, frame/hash and review status. Reused evidence retains its original source and explicit unchanged-input justification. Missing or rejected proof stays open. Existing title-map checks cannot establish this coverage alone.

The binding instructions are .claude/rules/es-ui-style-guide.md; the reference/evidence format is docs/es-menu-map.md. Current #508/#510 proof follows them.

Current qualification at 2026-10-08 02:31 UTC: distribution6f89bc7cecee5972909828103689e2c7c0711c30 and ESbaeea2a8c9bf508949104abcf04583a2338e054f remain local/unintegrated. Restore boundary controls pass21/21, validator controls30/30, ES182 cases/4727 assertions and changed-source linking. The final full host run20261008T021032Z-6981bf69 completed at02:18:59UTC: 1,311 top-level PASS, zeroFAIL/zeroSKIP, actual build/wrapper/launcher channels0; direct invocation has no inner.rc. Ordinary VM WebDAV and SFTP round trips each pass108 checks and all four completion channels. Earlier failed/withdrawn controls remain traceable in docs/qa-logs/2026-10-07-cloud-validator/.

Main UI proof has39 reviewed frames and two rejected frames. Independent review found additional help/error/diagnostic variants: supplemental indexed entries are being exercised by rc_cloud_ui on one new disposable source-overlay VM. The complete diff-derived inventory also covers changed scan/transfer continuation and connection callbacks. #512 records missing localization coverage for three introduced reasons plus an actual busy-check screen incorrectly labelled as synchronization; the narrow fix and affected French proof are in progress. The original guest and completed compiler scratch were retired with compact receipts. Review the complete affected copy/branch inventory before retiring the supplemental guest. The nested-folder warning is ordinary script stdout; consumer tracing must distinguish it from the actual displayed transfer result. Accepted firmware and its visual baseline remain unchanged.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: supplemental saves/settings/game-content help, rejected/unreadable path changes and nested-folder transfer outcomes use unchanged source plus synthetic WebDAV on GENERIC_X64. No physical-device or personal-cloud action is needed. Do not repeat the passing broad/ordinary VM suites without a new source change or concern.

D-WORKFLOW-156 now requires source, canonical flow/IA reference and reviewed indexed screenshots before UI completion or pin promotion, including text-only changes and each distinct affected content variant. Generic small-file organization remains an explicitly unresolved contract item; the maintainer’s scope question is pending. Next: close supplemental visual coverage, resolve that scope item, then integrate qualified source and proceed to #507. No product pin change or new device build has occurred.

## Canonical flow and screenshot reference — 2026-10-08

> We also ensured that we updated all of our documentation and our diagrams that serve as canonical reference points for all of the flows and information architecture of the app. The idea was also to use these as a way to store screenshots at each flow, so we know what the definitive happy path flows are and also what the branching edge cases are. We have a visual benchmark and baseline for what the entire experience throughout EmulationStation is meant to be.

D-WORKFLOW-155 reinforces D-UI-039/076: keep the canonical IA/menu map and affected flow diagrams together with reviewed happy-path and branching-case screenshots. docs/es-menu-map.md is the entrypoint; docs/pixelelated/cloud-folder-flow-review.md now holds the current implementation diagram and CF01–CF15 coverage table. Record trigger/outcome, source/build, language/panel and review status. Uncovered cases remain explicit. Reuse existing vm-walks/frame-diff; the accepted d72084ccad baseline remains unchanged. Draft VM overlays are not qualified firmware or an automatic baseline replacement.

- [ ] The final cloud-flow diagram and menu placement match the committed source; the evidence table links reviewed screenshots for happy path, manual instructions, independent path return, no selection, stale configuration, unreadable/retry, and creation decline/cancellation. Each gap or synthetic-only control is named explicitly.

Current source and exact qualification status are maintained above. No product pin, integration, new device firmware or baseline promotion has occurred.

## Active implementation — release lane resumed

> Sounds good, and we should trigger a new lane if you want, within Herdr, for website work. I want to keep us focused here in this lane on the critical path of getting the build completed. We were in the flow, trying to get everything done. Run the changes and adjustments for the release candidate to simplify the experience and expectations of what happens when connecting a new remote via rclone, and I don't want to lose that progress and momentum.

Website #511 now has a separate Herdr workspace, pixelelated · Website (wG:p1, agent pixelelated-web); its startup trust prompt is pending. This lane owns the firmware critical path. Distribution implementation resumes in m7-manual-cloud-folders; ES in m7-manual-cloud-setup. Root owns content restore boundaries/cache binding; scoped workers own validator/setup and ES UI. No new device build or product pin yet.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: source parser/transport controls use isolated synthetic host fixtures; controller flows, EN/FR640×480 and1280×800 frames use one disposable GENERIC_X64 guest. Qualified image adoption is still separate. No personal cloud or physical-device action is needed.

## Maintainer request

> Also, with the "tidy up your cloud folders," that only mattered once they'd linked a cloud backend. We should respect their choice in doing that. If they happen to choose a different folder, I didn't think we would move their ROMs around. If we need to add more clarity to our own flows and what tidying up is, we should think more about that. Moving around ROMs, as we found, can be a very data-intensive operation, and so we might want to delineate between organizing or moving ROMs versus all of the other files we deal with. We're not finding ourselves in a situation where we're trying to use a handheld with a limited CPU to move hundreds of GB of files.

## Current and historical behavior

#508/D-CLOUD-175 removes cloud relocation from 0.0.1 setup. Linking and explicit folder selection preserve existing cloud files; users arrange their library independently. The later request below promotes this to a pre-build flow review. Product integration and new device firmware are held; existing synthetic proof may finish. No tidier is reintroduced by this review.

The pre-hard-fork distribution PR3404 (4c83ebede4) already included content relocation when its path matched a derived old layout. Its recovery branch also inferred an old content path from a /Content suffix. Custom sibling-layout/path guards existed, but a folder-name heuristic is not reliable evidence of user intent. The ES tidier label emphasized saves/settings. Historical source/PR40 remain evidence; both submitted PRs closed unmerged.

Any future optional organization must distinguish saves/settings from ROMs/BIOS/game content, respect explicit folder choices and remain opt-in after connection. Choosing a backend or folder is not permission to rearrange its contents. A ROM-library move needs separate named source/destination, file/byte estimate, collision/preservation policy and transport explanation. Do not silently fall back from a provider-side operation to transferring/verifying hundreds of GB through the handheld; propose a computer/provider route when capability is absent or uncertain.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: synthetic bounded fixtures, including content that exists only in the cloud, can prove planning/consent/refusal behavior. Backend transport guarantees require capability/source evidence and controlled observations; no owner's library is needed.

## Pre-build review request

> But before we get too close and generate another build for a device, I want to review what our expectations are around reorganization, the flow, and how this works. For example, we need to think about if a user should be able to have their ROMs in a different directory or not. We could let the user select a different directory for their ROMs, or we could create the structure and instruct them to move their ROMs into the folder that's waiting for them.
>
> With the tidying up, we should think about what that does, because I actually don't remember right now if it touches ROM files at all and how it's currently structured or not. If we restrict it just to game saves, save states, and screenshots, that might be fine.
>
> Again, no one has used anything we've built, including what was opened as PRs to ROCKNIX, so they'll be coming from the current version of ROCKNIX. No one will be upgrading like I am, so we should not do anything to accommodate me. The only thing we should do is revert or clean up my folder after we attempted to do the migration from /ROCKNIX to /pixelelated.

D-CLOUD-177: current public ROCKNIX plus clean installs are the adoption baseline. Official release20261001/tagc445081a59518f37d9776e5412dd7b14910696f7 uses /GAMES and /GAMES/backup; it does not install our optional tidier or content transfer helpers. Unpublished fork states remain historical evidence, not product compatibility gates. The owner's cloud reconciliation remains separate and private.

Review artifact: docs/pixelelated/cloud-folder-flow-review.md. Exact-source findings: the old tidier moves derived ROM content and its saves relocation is not restricted by the normal progress allowlist. Current independent CONTENT_REMOTE selection moves no files but is exposed only inside a conditional restore chooser; it lacks recursive navigation. General CHANGE CLOUD FOLDER overwrites all three sibling pointers. Content restore has fallbacks outside the selected root, while backup always writes ROMs/<system> and BIOS. The draft also retains a player warning pointing at the removed TIDY action. These boundaries must match the agreed flow before integration.

The subsequent decision D-CLOUD-178 below chooses a validator, explicit smaller-file fixes and manual ROM/BIOS instructions. The earlier alternatives are historical design context, not a pending request to choose again.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The review records the official release/tag and actual configuration/package/filter bytes that establish the public ROCKNIX adoption baseline; unpublished fork states are separated from required compatibility.
- [ ] D-CLOUD-178 and the flow diagram specify enabled-category checks, supported selected-root layout, independent pointer preservation and explicit actions; no stale "awaiting owner choice" instruction remains in current plans.
- [ ] The small-file action contract names recognized cases, exact plan/consent, file count/bytes, collision and source-retention behavior, stale-plan refusal, interruption and verification costs; no ROM/BIOS/settings archive/unknown-file relocation is hidden inside it.
- [ ] #508 criteria, menu map, current docs and synthetic test plan match read-only validation and manual ROM/BIOS guidance before integration or a new device build. Actual VM proof distinguishes missing from unreadable and preserves unselected and unrelated files.
- [ ] M7 and the canonical checkpoint put #510 contract reconciliation before #508 qualification/integration and #507 audit; #511 website/QR guides run separately without holding local guidance or adding a firmware release gate.

## Additional owner options: enabled features and category checks

> Well, another option is to create the folder and use it for the bits we enable. If they'd like to use it for ROMs, we should then make a decision about whether they would need to move their ROMs into that directory first or choose their own.
>
> For simplicity's sake, we might just say that once you link an Arcclone backend, we create the structure for them and then ask them to move things into those directories. All our tool does is give away that, once they've migrated the content in, it validates it. At that point, we could tidy things up because everything's already in the directory, so we shouldn't be moving anything around.
>
> Alternatively, we could offer strictly the tidy-up, save states, game saves, and screenshots. Another option would be to tell them what's not passing and have it be a series of checks. If they want to fix it, we could offer the option to fix that content type. This would be similar to what we do with the restore, where we let them choose from several options. We would just allow them to organize and let them select what they want to organize, and then the burden is on the user, not on us.

The review document now compares fixed folders for enabled features plus category checks against an independent existing-library location. A successful validation makes no organization changes. An optional fix still names the concrete operation and scope; basic layout/access checks cannot establish full transfer integrity without trusted inventory/hash evidence, and must not silently download a whole library. The later D-CLOUD-178 decision below supersedes the choice among these options. Prior synthetic QA is sealed and its disposable resources are retired; implementation must now match that validator contract.

## Chosen direction: validator, explicit fixes and instructions

> Yes, this is where I think a validator is probably the way to go. Now we can offer a fix for smaller file types, and then we can deal with some edge cases that we know will likely happen. For example, if the ROMs aren't present at all, or if they're not in the right directory but present, I think the same would be true for the BIOS files. We can then also point them to look online for documentation on how to set everything up for those two types.

> A validator would also be helpful, and we may actually already have the building blocks in our restore and backup functions because we already have interface elements and checks around this.

> We also shouldn't have a link that is expected to be clickable. We could show a QR code, though.

> We need to build out our site, so this can be a future task we define now and tackle later. Once the site's live, we could have this on the wiki. It would take someone directly to the setup guide, and we could then have one for their ROMs and one for BIOS files. Instead of a fix button, it would say "See instructions" or something akin to that, and that would then show a QR code in a modal to take them to the page to fix it.

D-CLOUD-178 selects category validation. Reads remain scoped to enabled categories and selected roots, with present/empty/missing/misplaced/unreadable findings tied to the checked configuration. Missing at the expected path is not cloud-wide absence; layout readiness is not transfer integrity or BIOS compatibility. Reuse readers/classifiers and existing scan/category/QR presentation, without invoking backup/restore transfers as checks.

Explicit smaller-file fixes are limited to game saves, save states and screenshots, with a concrete preview, size/count, collision/preservation policy and verification contract before implementation. There is no existing safe category repair API to call wholesale. ROM/BIOS findings show expected paths and manual instructions. Once #511 publishes verified guide destinations, **See instructions** opens the corresponding ROM or BIOS QR modal. Keep local guidance useful before publication and offline; no dead URLs or clickable handheld links.

#511 is now a parallel GitHub Pages/site planning track after the owner's follow-up, not an added firmware RC gate. Earlier pre-validator drafts were distribution3268015c and ES300f97d2. Their clipping, selected-root fallbacks, coupled pointers and obsolete TIDY warning are resolved in the qualified source above. Product integration remains held for the explicit repair-scope decision; those older drafts are historical evidence, not current build inputs.
